newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia mass murderer used surfing alibi.
newsitem.headline: Australia mass murderer used surfing alibi.

text.p: Australian mass murderer Martin Bryant said he had been surfing and knew nothing about the shooting massacre of 35 people when police arrested him shortly after the killings, a court was told on Wednesday.
Prosecutor Nick Perks told the Tasmanian Supreme Court that Bryant -- who now admits the murders -- showed a complete lack of remorse and claimed he had been unjustly accused.

Perks said Bryant was asked in his first police interview after his arrest what he knew about the massacre on April 28 at the historic convict site of Port Arthur in the southeast coast of the island state of Tasmania.
"Bryant's response...was that he did not know anything, that he was a long way from Port Arthur surfing," Perks said. "I have been unjustly accused," Perks quoted Bryant as saying.
Bryant drove to the murder scene in a yellow Volvo car with a surfboard tied to the roof.
In preparing to play a video tape police interview with Bryant, Perks said the recording "demonstratively shows his complete lack of remorse".
Two weeks ago, Bryant confessed to murdering 35 people at Port Arthur and also pleaded guilty to 20 attempted murders, but he has yet to give any reason for his actions.
Bryant is appearing in court for a sentencing hearing which is expected to continue through Thursday. The prosecution has asked the judge to jail Bryant for life, without parole.

On Tuesday, the court was told that Bryant took less than two minutes to slaughter 20 people, all at point-blank or close range as they ate their lunch at the Broad Arrow Cafe at Port Arthur. He later hunted victims in the nearby bush, executing a six-year-old girl as she hid behind a tree.
The court heard Bryant had planned his massacre for months.
